question: to the Commission Cristina Guarda (Verts/ALE), Isabel Serra Sánchez (The Left), Evin Incir (S&D) Subject:

AngloGold Ashanti, a global gold-mining company with European investment, has been conducting prospecting and mining exploration in Jericó, in the Antioquia region of Colombia, since 2002. The company aims to establish a mining district to extract copper, gold, silver and their concentrates. Numerous small-scale farmers and their families live and work in the area intended for the mining project, growing coffee, avocados and other foods for their own sustenance. Since the announcement of the mining project in the region, those who have voiced criticism of it have been subjected to stigmatisation tactics and disinformation campaigns aimed at intimidating them. The situation escalated when AngloGold Ashanti filed a criminal complaint in 2025 against 11 peasant leaders, accusing them of kidnapping, aggravated theft and personal injury, simply for exercising their right to peaceful protest. The next hearing will take place in August 2026. In this context we would like to ask the Commission: 1.
Does the EU Delegation in Bogotá have any plans to visit the affected communities to ensure that the company is complying fully with European standards on due diligence and human rights?
How does the EU Delegation intend to monitor the legal proceedings against the farmers, in line with its obligations under the guidelines on human rights defenders and the Anti-SLAPP Directive?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (13.8.2026) The EU Delegation to Colombia closely follows the situation in Jericó, including through the project ‘The Right to Defend Rights’, under which one of its implementing partners, the Corporación Jurídica Libertad, has provided legal defence to the farmers facing criminal proceedings and conducted advisory and support visits to the affected community. As part of the project, a podcast episode is also being prepared to raise awareness of the situation in Jericó. Officials of the European External Action Service also met with the Coordinator of the Mesa Ambiental de Jericó in June 2026, during his visit to Brussels to participate in a meeting of the European Parliament delegation for relations with the countries of the Andean Community, entitled ‘Voices of Human Rights Defenders in Andean Communities – Technical perspective, international framework and testimonies’. The EU, including its Delegation in Bogotá, will continue to maintain regular dialogue with civil society organisations and implementing partners of EU-funded initiatives to stay informed about developments on the ground.
